Just to clarify, this video was never meant to be racist in any way. I was speaking purely from an artistic perspective. As I'm starting to learn coloring, I naturally find some skin tones more challenging to render than others. That doesn't mean I like them any less. In fact, both my mom's and my dad's sides of the family are Black. My mom herself has dark skin, so why would I dislike the same skin tone as my own family? The same goes for hair textures. I have naturally curly/coily hair, and from an artistic point of view, I personally find it more difficult to draw and render than straight hair. That doesn't mean I don't like it—in fact, I love my hair. It's simply about the technical challenge of drawing and coloring different features, nothing more. Please don't confuse artistic difficulty with personal preference or prejudice. They're two completely different things.  #dessin #black #fyp #drawing #fypシ゚

I tried something a little different today — a blueprint-style colouring page. First, I filled the entire page with my huge blue marker, going horizontal, vertical, and in circles to get a really even, non-patchy background. Then I drew a grid over the whole page, coloured the lines white, and added little details like lines, measurements, and text to mimic a real blueprint. Honestly, the process wasn’t quite as fun as I had imagined 😅 but the result turned out pretty cool and graphic, so I’m still happy with it. What do you think — does it actually look like a blueprint? And would you try this technique yourself? #coloringpage #coloringtechnique #blueprinteffect #creativecoloring #artprocess

videos.caption: Okay, so this one is a slightly more intermediate tutorial, but (like all things) it is so beautiful once you put in the work. You'll need 4 shades of the same color (from light to dark), 1 colored pencil in a similar color (optional), and 1 fine-tip white marker or gel pen. Things to keep in mind: * you'll be working from lightest to darkest * for the wispy, feather-like strokes, hold your markers upright and NOT on an angle (holding upright will give you more a more finer stroke, holding on an angle will produce a broader stroke which isn't what we're going for) * colored pencil is optional but I feel like it ties the look together, feel free to omit if you don't find it necessary.
